full_judgment: 2. The facts giving rise to the Rule, in brief, are that the petitioner Abdur Rahman Munshi along with other instituted OS No. 353 of 1974 in the 2nd Court of Munsif at Netrokona for permanent injunction against the opposite parties and others restraining them from entering in the lands described in the schedule appended to the plaint of the suit. At first ad-interim injunction was issued against the defendants but subsequently the learned Munsif rejected the prayer of the temporary injunction and vacated the order of the ad-interim injunction. Against the order of the learned Munsif rejecting the prayer of the temporary injunction, Miscellaneous Appeal No. 71 of 1975 was filed in the Court of the District Judge on 25-3-75. On 1-4-75 the petitioner along with others filed complaint with the Officer-in-charge of Kaliajuri Police Station stating about apprehension of the breach of peace, and on the basis of the report filed by the police the Sub-Divisional Officer issued order under section 144 of the code of Criminal Procedure against the opposite parties restraining them from entering in the disputed land. On 14-4-75, on the basis of the petition filed by the petitioner under section 144 CrPC records of both the cases were combined and the proceeding under section 145 of Code of Criminal Procedure was drawn up attaching the land and appointing a receiver. The Miscellaneous Appeal preferred by the petitioner and others in the Court of the District Judge against refusal of temporary injunction by the learned Munsif was heard by the Additional Sub-ordinate Judge, Mymensingh who, on 24-1-76, allowed the appeal and restrained the OPs 2-4 from entering in the disputed land. Against the decision of the learned Additional Sub-ordinate Judge the OPs 2-4 filed a Revision Case bearing the No. 381 of 1976 in the High Court which is still pending. On 13-2-76, the petitioner and others filed a petition before the Sub-Divisional Officer, Netrokona for dropping the proceeding under section 145 of Code of Criminal Procedure on the ground that the Additional Sub-ordinate Judge restrained the opposite parties 2-4 by an order of temporary injunction from entering in the disputed land on the basis of his judgment dated 24-1-76 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 71 of 1975, but the learned Sub-Divisional Magistrate rejected the prayer for dropping the proceeding. Against the order of Sub-Divisional Magistrate, the petitioner and others filed Motion No. 216 of 1976 in the Court of the Sessions Judge. The Additional Sessions judge, Mymensingh who heard the Motion rejected the Motion. Hence the petitioner Abdur Rahman Munshi filed the present Revisional Application in this Court on 22-1-79 and obtained the Rule. The petitioner Abdur Rahman Munshi filed a supplementary affidavit stating that the OS 353 of 1974 was decreed on 8-8-79, and hence the proceedings under section 145 CrPC should be dropped. A counter affidavit on behalf of the OP No. 2 was filed stating that OP obtained a rule in Civil Revision No. 381 of 1976 from the High Court Division on 22-3-76 and the record of the suit was called for but the Court concerned instead of sending the record to the High Court Division sent the record to the Court of Munsif who did not inform the Advocate of the OP No. 2 who was engaged by him in the court of the Munsif of Netrokona about receipt of the record, and the plaintiffs of the OS No. 353 of 1974 fraudulently managed to secure the ex-parte decree without the knowledge of the OPs. The OPs 2-4 filed a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX rule 13 for setting aside the decree which is still pending. A copy of the application under Order IX rule 13 CPC has been made Annexure 'A' in the counter-affidavit filed by the OP No. 2. That application it was stated that after issuing a rule on 23-3-1976 in the Civil Revision No. 381 of 1976, the High Court called for the record of the suit for which the present OPs 2-4 did not go to the Court of the Munsif honestly believing that the records of the Munsif's Court would he sent to the High Court, but to their to their utter surprise they learnt from their Advocate in the High Court Division on 8-2-80 that the suit had been decreed ex-parte on 25-7-79. It is further stated in the application under Order IX, rule 13 CPC that the Munsif, 2nd Court, Netrokona received the records of OS No. 353 of 1974 after disposal of the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 71 of 1975 on 14-1-76 and 11-1-76 was fixed as the date of hearing with the direction to inform the Advocates of both the sides but unfortunately the learned lawyer of defendants was not informed about the order of the Court for which the preset OPs 2-4 and their Advocate was unaware of the further proceedings in OS No. 353 of 1974 and the ex-parte decree was passed without their knowledge.
